run: poll: random phase, SPIRE agent sync_interval and server cache_reload_interval both 1 s
headline: vend_to_access_ms: P sends POST /delegations (t0) -> C receives the resource's first 200 for GET /datasets/A with its own JWT-SVID
child_behaviour: C runs `parentsim access-wait -access-style=poll` before the vend: every 20 ms it fetches a JWT-SVID (audience spiffe://lab.local/svc/resource, one-shot) and, once one for its vended ID arrives, sends GET /datasets/A with it in the same tick, until the first 200. Measures when access first becomes possible.
harness: src/experiments/vend_to_access.py (reusing vend_to_svid.py's parts), parentsim modes vend-timed and access-wait

code.state: uncommitted working tree at run time

command: cd src/experiments && CLUSTER_NAME=nhi-lab KUBECTX=kind-bench-v2a-1s TRUST_DOMAIN=lab.local uv run python3 vend_to_access.py --style poll --trials 50 --jitter-s 5 --run-id 20261102T040134Z-vend-to-access-poll-1s

cluster.kind_cluster: bench-v2a-1s (throwaway, two nodes), created for the two vend-to-access runs and deleted after them
bring_up: make policy-engine-up vending-service-up resource-up experiments-fixtures-up KIND_CLUSTER=bench-v2a-1s
cluster.note: the runs were started without make, because the make targets re-apply the repository's SPIRE ConfigMaps

config_changes_on_this_cluster_only.change: in the server block of the live spire-server ConfigMap: `audit_log_enabled = true` and `experimental { cache_reload_interval = "1s" }` (default 5 s); StatefulSet restarted
in the agent block of the live spire-agent ConfigMap: `experimental { sync_interval = "1s" }` (default 5 s); DaemonSet restarted after the server

smoke_run: 2 trials of each style passed every check before the 50-trial runs, on the same cluster and config

logs.window: contiguous per trial: from the end of the previous trial's window (the first starts 1 s before trial 1) to the moment C held no identity again after the dispose
logs.timestamp: first field of each line: the container runtime's capture time (kubectl logs --timestamps); for parent/, the time this host received P's command output
